representative: Type-level profile (HPV16, reference K02718, the ICTV exemplar of its species). Particle size and capsid architecture are family-level ICTV values.
summary: A small, non-enveloped virus whose capsid is built from 72 five-fold capsomers of the L1 protein. It carries a circular double-stranded DNA genome and completes its life cycle only as infected skin or mucosal cells differentiate.

taxonomy.note: MSL41 places papillomaviruses in the realm Floreoviria; older sources (before MSL41) list a different realm. The species name has not been converted to binomial format in MSL41. HPV16 is a papillomavirus 'type', a level below species.

hostDetail.value: Vertebrates (ICTV host-source category); infects epithelial cells

sense.note: Sense applies to single-stranded RNA genomes; a dsDNA genome has two complementary template strands.

lengthKb.note: Papillomavirus genomes span 5,748–8,607 bp across the family (ICTV).

capsid.value: Icosahedral capsid of 72 pentameric L1 capsomers in a T=7 arrangement (360 L1 copies), with the minor protein L2.

dimensions.label: Capsid diameter
dimensions.note: The ICTV profile table gives 55 nm; the ICTV Report text gives ~600 Å (60 nm).

site.note: Our ICTV sources describe epithelial replication but the fetched text did not state the compartment explicitly; nuclear replication is standard teaching and is flagged for verification.

mRNARoute.value: As a dsDNA virus, the genome is transcribed directly into mRNA.

steps.title: Initial amplification
steps.text: After entry, the genome is amplified with the viral E1 helicase (the only viral enzyme) and E2.

steps.title: Maintenance
steps.text: The genome is maintained at low copy number in dividing cells, associated with host chromosomes during mitosis.

steps.title: Differentiation-dependent amplification
steps.text: As cells differentiate in the upper epithelium, viral DNA is amplified to high copy number; E6 and E7 help the virus replicate in these cells.

steps.title: Assembly and release
steps.text: Capsid proteins L1 and L2 assemble around the DNA; virions are released as cells slough off.
